write_status: reviewed-only; no production insert authorized until image corrections, transport taxonomy, guarded migration and rollback pass isolated PostgreSQL dry-run
review_method: Confirmed project identity, completion, place, architect and transport program against architect, operator or municipality sources.
Queried production buildings and found no canonical building match for the three target identities.
Queried Commons through the MediaWiki API for author, own-work or Flickr provenance, dimensions, current license and source URL.
Opened all three current images and the proposed CASE-094 replacement at original detail for manual building-content verification.
Rejected the current CASE-094 rail-yard view as a canonical primary image even though its Commons metadata names the station.
Required a new transport-hub function instead of misclassifying stations and a passenger terminal as generic mixed-use buildings.

taxonomy_prerequisite.reason: All three buildings are primarily passenger-transport nodes; existing mixed-use or community-center functions would be semantically wrong.

canonical_building.name_zh: 女川站与女川温泉 Yupoppo
canonical_building.name_en: Onagawa Station and Onagawa Onsen Yupoppo
canonical_building.name_ja: 女川駅舎・女川温泉温浴施設ゆぽっぽ

identity_evidence: Shigeru Ban Architects records a completed 2015 new-built station in Japan.
The official description confirms the three-storey railway and public-bath complex, curved LVL lattice roof and membrane structure visible in the reviewed image.

image.visual_evidence: Clear frontal exterior shows the Onagawa JR and yupoppo signage, three-storey facade and curved white roof.
image.rights_evidence: MediaWiki API reports own work by Mister0124 under CC BY-SA 4.0.

identity_evidence: Kengo Kuma and Associates identifies the completed Tokyo infrastructure project and its large membrane roof supported by origami-shaped steel and cedar frames.

The station opened in March 2020; the architect page currently lists March 2021 completion for the full project, so year_start remains the public opening year while the evidence note preserves this distinction.

image.credit: Photo: 江戸村のとくぞう / Wikimedia Commons
image.visual_evidence: Clear daylight exterior shows the station elevation, white membrane roof, steel frame and glazed concourse. The current CASE image is rejected because it primarily shows a night rail yard.
image.rights_evidence: MediaWiki API reports own work by 江戸村のとくぞう under CC BY-SA 4.0.

canonical_building.name_ja: 横浜港大さん橋国際客船ターミナル

identity_evidence: The terminal operator and City of Yokohama confirm the current seventh-generation international passenger terminal completed in 2002, with a public rooftop plaza and passenger facilities.
JA and MoMA identify Foreign Office Architects, Farshid Moussavi and Alejandro Zaera-Polo as the design authors.

image.visual_evidence: Exact rooftop plaza view shows the terminal's continuous timber public landscape, folded roof forms and cruise-ship berth.
image.rights_evidence: MediaWiki API reports own work by Syced dedicated under CC0.
